collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Children and elders plant a garden with a plant from every family: let each family choose, or plant what grows best.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) are planting a garden in the middle of the village with one plant from every family: a grandmother's favorite flower, a fisher's medicine herb, a child's watermelon. (friend) worries some of the plants will not grow together. (subject) says that is not the point. What should they plant?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every family brings its plant. Some thrive. Some sulk. One family brings a seed nobody can identify, and it grows into a vine that tries to eat the meeting hut. The garden is a beautiful mess.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They plant only what will grow well together. The garden is lovely and tidy. A few families are disappointed their plant was left out. (subject) plants those in a pot by (subject.his/her) door.
